title: Rigidity at the Extremal Crouzeix Constant
content: For a complex matrix \(A\), let \(\psi(A)\) be the norm of its polynomial functional calculus on the numerical range. We prove that \(\psi(A)=2\) forces the numerical range to be a nondegenerate closed disk. Equality in the sharp double-layer estimate gives a boundary-kernel identity for a finite Blaschke extremizer. A curved exposed arc turns this identity into a rational formula, and a resolvent argument identifies the full unit lemniscate with the numerical-range boundary. The associated tangent polynomial divides a Hermitian determinant. Its real roots correspond to the two support lines in a generic direction, forcing a conic; the points at infinity then make it a circle. In every fixed finite dimension at least two, we also prove that a proper convex domain has scalar domain constant two exactly when it is a disk. Compactness yields uniform near-equality rigidity up to translation and positive scaling, and a uniform gap for unbounded domains.
